understanding.bridge: The LinkedIn feed you stopped opening is what the Upanishads call the mind running after another's shadow.
understanding.week_thesis: The feed you stopped opening is the thing that keeps you stuck. The week is about closing it, measuring your own path, and taking one step that is yours.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the shame of being left behind and the habit of looking at what others have.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the feed is not neutral. It is designed to make you feel behind by showing you what you do not yet have.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your path is not measured by where someone else is.
week_beats.act: You try closing the feed and writing one thing you did today that moved you forward.
week_beats.story: A young person who sent out more than they could count shows you how to find footing without looking up.

queries.hook: The weight of watching peers pull ahead while you are stuck in a job that does not fit, and the shame of hiding from the feed that shows them.
queries.diagnose: Measuring your life against another's success burns at their win and steals the contentment in your own path; the more you look, the more the mind wants to look.
queries.steady: What is yours to build is not measured by where someone else is; no honest effort on the right path is ever wasted.
queries.act: Walk your own path, even imperfectly, rather than someone else's well; be grateful for what is yours and rejoice in others' good.
queries.story: A young person who sent out more than they could count, faced the silence, and found their footing not by looking up but by turning inward.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in the middle of a field, unsure, watching the lives of others. Krishna tells him that the work born of your own nature is the only work that will not eat you alive. He says it is better to walk your own path with all its cracks than to perform another's role with perfect polish. The truth is that every path has flaws, and your only job is to do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.for_you: The applications you sent out are your own path, even if the replies have not come. The work of making flat whites is your work, done with your own hands. Do that work today, not as a step down, but as the honest offering it is.

verse.speaker: Bali
verse.setting: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his fallen rival Bali living as a donkey and mocks him.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेतदनुरूपं ते यशसो वा कुलस्य च / समृद्धार्थोऽसमृद्धार्थं यन्मां कत्थितुमिच्छसि
verse.line: Gloating over someone who has fallen says more about you than about them.
verse.translation: It does not suit your reputation or your family that you, who have everything, should wish to boast over me, who have lost it.
verse.why: Success is on loan. Don't gloat in a good season or despair in a bad one.

prasang.title: Bali and Indra: the fortune that moves on
prasang.summary: Indra, now king of the gods, finds his defeated rival Bali living as a donkey in an empty house and mocks him. Bali calmly answers that fortune has lived with a thousand Indras before, that time gives and takes, and that this is a season for calm.
prasang.story_hook: The king of the gods went looking for his old enemy and found him living as a donkey.
prasang.lesson: Success is on loan. Don't gloat in a good season or despair in a bad one.

verse.meaning: Indra, the new king of the gods, finds his old rival Bali living as a donkey in an empty house. He mocks him. Bali answers that it does not suit Indra's reputation or his family to boast over a man who has lost everything. The verse shows that success is on loan. It comes and goes with time. Gloating over someone who has fallen says more about you than about them.
verse.for_you: Your friends at Goldman and Deloitte are just a season. The feed is not a neutral mirror. It is a stage built to make you feel behind by showing you what you do not yet have.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verse.sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
verse.translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
verse.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasang.title: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on how a wise person lives and works. He says that a person who is content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, and free from envy, remains steady in success and failure. Even when they are acting, they are not bound. The point is that contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.
verse.for_you: When you see your friends at Goldman or Deloitte, you are measuring your path against theirs. This verse says your freedom is in being content with your own unasked-for steps. Your path is not measured by where they are. You can hold that steady.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From 'The Way of the Free Ascetic'.
verse.sanskrit: ब्रह्माण्डं मण्डलीमात्रं किं लोभाय मनस्विनः । शफरीस्फुरितेनाब्धिः क्षुब्धो न खलु जायते ॥
verse.line: The ocean is not stirred by a small fish's flick. Petty things needn't shake you.
verse.translation: For the high-minded the whole universe is a mere ring; what is there in it to be greedy for? The ocean is not churned up by the flicker of a little fish.
verse.why: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: The way of the free ascetic
prasang.summary: Portraits of the wandering sage: unbothered when people argue over his caste, sleeping under the sky like a king, and finally bidding farewell to the five elements.
prasang.lesson: Let others' labels and small things pass; contentment makes you rich.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from 'The Way of the Free. He says the high-minded see the whole universe as a mere ring, something not worth being greedy. He says the ocean is not churned up by the flicker of a little fish. The verse proposes that petty things and others' labels need not shake you, and that contentment makes you rich.
verse.for_you: Those flat whites you make are a flicker in the ocean of the world. Let the flicker go. Your path is not measured by the flicker of another's success.

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणान्येव सेवते / सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः
verse.line: Let go of envy and stay grateful, and good things keep finding their way to you.
verse.translation: The person who is free of envy and grateful keeps to what is good, and finds happiness, right living, prosperity and heaven.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.meaning: In the town of Mithila, a wise meat-seller named Dharmavyadha speaks to a proud ascetic named Kaushika. The ascetic has looked down on ordinary life, and the butcher shows him that true goodness is found in simple, honest work. The butcher says to let go of envy and stay grateful, because then good things keep finding their way to you. It is a quiet truth, spoken while selling meat, that a clear heart is enough.
verse.for_you: Your friends at Goldman and Deloitte are not the measure of your day. Write down one small thing you did today that moved you forward. It can be as simple as making a perfect flat white or sending out one solid application. That is your path, not theirs.

verse.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verse.setting: The sage warns the deposed prince against resenting others' success.
verse.sanskrit: सहस्व श्रियमन्येषां यद्यपि त्वयि नास्ति सा / अन्यत्रापि सतीं लक्ष्मीं कुशला भुञ्जते नराः / अभिनिष्यन्दते देही श्रीभूतश्च द्विषज्जनात्
verse.line: Make peace with other people's success, even when you lack it. The wise can enjoy good fortune that isn't theirs.
verse.translation: Bear the good fortune of others, even though it is not with you. Wise people know how to enjoy good fortune even when it belongs to someone else; good fortune drains away from the one who resents.
verse.why: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

script: You are stuck and ashamed. You look at your phone and you see your friends at Goldman and Deloitte. You see the flat whites you are making and you feel small. You sent out those applications but the replies have not come yet. You are measuring yourself against their lives and it is eating you alive.

Arjuna stands in the middle of a field, his bow heavy in his hands, watching the lives of others. Krishna stands beside him and sees the doubt in his eyes. Arjuna is watching the armies of his own kin and he feels the weight of a duty that is not his. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna tells him that the work born of your own nature is the only work that will not eat you alive. He says it is better to walk your own path with all its cracks than to perform another's role with perfect polish. The truth is that every path has flaws. Your only job is to do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

The applications you sent out are your own path, even if the replies have not come. The work of making flat whites is your work, done with your own hands. Do that work today, not as a step down, but as the honest offering it is.
Walk your own path with all its cracks.

depth.life: You are making flat whites and sending out applications, but your mind drifts to other people's wins. You feel ashamed and stuck, as if your own life is disappearing behind everyone else's success.
depth.points: You are not stuck because you cannot get in. You are stuck because every time you look, someone else's win is the only thing you see, and your own life disappears behind it.
depth.practice: Notice when your mind compares you to others today. Then bring your attention back to the work in your hands, the one that fits you.
depth.question: What is one small thing you did today that fits your own nature?
